Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · School & learning

source noun

a person, book or record that information comes from

also sources, reliable source, informant

classical

Cic. Att. 14.8.1: certīs auctōribus comperisse
Ov. Fast. 5.601: nōn dubiīs auctōribus

auctor, auctōris m./f.

an informant, an authority; the writer one follows

A historian names his source with auctor est (see according to).

Other words

  • fōns, fontis m. — a source (a work one draws on)

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. source (a book or other work supplying information)

    Classically a figure: to draw from the springs, not chase the rivulets (Cic. Ac. 1.8, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • quibus in extrēmīs erat sibi īnsidiās fierī; sē id certīs auctōribus comperisse

    at the end of which he said that a plot was being laid against him, and that he had it from reliable sourcesCic. Att. 14.8.1

  • tum mihi nōn dubiīs auctōribus incipit aestās

    then, on no doubtful authority, my summer beginsOv. Fast. 5.601

See also according to, source, author.

SourcesLewis & Short: auctor · Lewis & Short: fons

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. source (a book or other work supplying information).
